fit_ellipses.compute_central_moment_tensors_full()¶

Compute a central moment tensor (u) for every cell (simple polygons, 0th, 1st and 2nd moments) Based on Mulchrone and Choudhury, J. of Structural Geology 26 (2004)

Parameters:
  • moment_tensors (numpy array) – Array of 3X3 tensors for every cell
  • points (numpy array) – Coordinates of Voronoi centers
  • areas (numpy array) – Areas of Voronoi cells
Returns:

central_moment_tensors – Array of 3X3 central moment tensors for every cell
Return type:

numpy array
fit_ellipses.compute_ellipse_parameters()¶

Compute the fitted ellipses for every cell using the central moment tensors Based on Mulchrone and Choudhury, J. of Structural Geology 26 (2004)

Parameters:central_moment_tensors (numpy array) – Array of 3X3 central moment tensors for every cell
Returns:
  • semi_minor_axes (numpy array) – Semi minor axes of the fitted ellipse
  • semi_major_axes (numpy array) – Semi major axes of the fitted ellipse
  • angles_alpha (numpy array) – Angles (in radian) between the major axis of the fitted ellipse and the positive x-axis

fit_ellipses.ellipse_Hiraiwa()¶
fit_ellipses.fit_ellipses_to_cells()¶

Compute the “best fit” ellipse to Voronoi cells (or any polygons) using their moment tensors and their central moment tensors.

Parameters:
  • regions (list of lists) – Indices of vertices in each revised Voronoi regions.
  • vertices (numpy array) – Coordinates of cell vertices
  • points (numpy array) – Coordinates of Voronoi centers
  • areas (numpy array) – Areas of Voronoi cells
  • debug (boolean) – When true, compute angles between the major axis and the x-axis with and without an absolute value on the denominator.
  • plot_on (boolean) – When true, plots the ellipses on a graph
Returns:

  • semi_minor_axes (numpy array) – Semi minor axes of the fitted ellipse
  • semi_major_axes (numpy array) – Semi major axes of the fitted ellipse
  • angles_alpha (numpy array) – Angles (in radian) between the major axis of the fitted ellipse and the positive x-axis. Returns the no_abs angles when debug=True
fit_ellipses.plot_ellipse()¶

Assumes that we possess every parameter, this is purely a plotting function. Note for Ellipse: width = total length (diameter) of horizontal axis height = total length (diameter) of vertical axis angle = rotation ink
